summary: counter.top must return the same entries in the same order for the same input, and n == 0 must mean every entry rather than none.
reason: The counter is backed by a Go map, whose iteration order the runtime randomises, so the sort is the only thing that makes intel output reproducible. Three rules carry that: descending Count, ties broken by ascending Label, and a limit that truncates only when n is positive and smaller than the result. A reprint must keep all three, and must not treat the zero limit as an empty result, because sponsors.go asks for a complete class distribution that way. Guarded by TestCounterTopLimitBoundaries, TestCounterTopBreaksTiesAlphabetically and TestCounterTopTieOrderIsStableAcrossRuns.
validated_outcome: Against the tests that existed before the new file, the limit rule and the tie-break rule both survived mutation: n > 0 to n >= 0 and Label i < j to i > j each left the package green, while the Count comparison flip failed 3 existing tests as a control. Against the new file all four mutations fail, including dropping the blank-key skip in add, which admits an empty label into the ranking.
